description: Dr. Bob Sports review, checked 7 Nov 2026: NFL only pricing, no refunds for losing picks, the long record he publishes himself, and what bettors say.
dek: Bob Stoll has sold model based picks as Dr. Bob since 1987. This season he sells only NFL plays, at $895 for the rest of the season or $375 for four weeks, with no refund if they lose. He publishes long season by season records, but he keeps them himself and the totals do not match from page to page.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record of Dr. Bob's plays. The records on this page are the ones his own site publishes. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: Dr. Bob Sports is a real, long running business run by one named analyst, Bob Stoll. It lists a mailing address and phone number, publishes its prices and terms, and writes long free analysis of games. In that sense it is legitimate.

Whether a buyer makes money is a separate question. Dr. Bob publishes more than most sellers: season by season win, loss and push counts going back decades, profit in stars or units, losing seasons, and a recap of each week's paid plays with the line. But that record is kept by the seller, the totals differ slightly between his own pages, and we found no public log of every play with its release time that an outsider can audit.
Treat the record as the seller's own bookkeeping, more detailed than most, not as proof. If you buy, log each play with the line and time you received it, and compare it with his weekly recap.

guarantee: There is no guarantee. The refund policy says: "Refunds will not be issued based on performance but in some cases refunds are issued based on other circumstances," and points to the terms. The terms say a subscriber may cancel at any time "without refund for any prepaid fees," and that a recurring subscription stays active to the end of the paid period. We did not see the NFL product pages say whether those packages renew automatically.
In plain terms: if the picks lose, you keep the losses and the fee. That is at least clearer than a "guarantee" that only pays in more picks.

claims_note: The NFL numbers do not agree from page to page. On 7 Nov 2026 the NFL page headline showed Strong Opinions at 411-335-16, the recap lower on the same page showed 411-335-15, and the package box on the same page, the product page and the release page still showed 520-386-12 Best Bets and 404-333-16 Strong Opinions. The homepage still shows the 2016 to 2025 totals. Adding this season's posted 7-7-1 Best Bets and 16-10-1 Strong Opinions to the 2016 to 2025 totals on the past performance page gives 521-386-13 and 412-335-16, one game off the headline in each case. These are small gaps, but a record kept by hand on several pages is not an audited record.

The about page is out of date in places: it says he is embarking on his 33rd year in business and that the NFL plays won 59% since 2016 "through 2020", while the homepage says 38 years. It also says that 60% plus winners long term "is no longer possible for anyone", which is a fair warning for anyone reading high win rates elsewhere.

Profit is shown in stars or units, not dollars. The NFL page says Best Bets are 1.0 unit or higher and Strong Opinions are 0.5 unit plays. The past performance page also lists bad stretches, such as NFL Best Bets at 50.6% from 1999 through 2012, after which he says he stopped handicapping the NFL until a new model in 2016, and weak college football Best Bet seasons in 2023 and 2024. Publishing losing years is a point in his favor, but the seller still chooses how the record is presented.
record: What is independently verifiable: nothing we could open. We found no third party that holds a time stamped log of Dr. Bob's paid plays, no contest results run by an organizer, and no regulator or court record about the business. Old forum posts from 2011 and 2012 discuss his yearly win rates, but they quote his own numbers.

What the seller publishes, and how a buyer could check it: the past performance page has season by season tables (wins, losses, pushes and stars, split by star rating for college football and basketball), and the NFL page posts a recap of the week's paid plays with the side or total, the line and the result, for example a 0.5 unit play on Detroit -3 -115 that won 19-15. This is more detail than most pick sellers show. But we saw only the current week's recap and season totals, not a complete dated archive of every play with its release time and line, and the release page is locked to subscribers. A buyer can check it only going forward: record each play with the line and the time you receive it, and compare with the weekly recap and the season total he posts.
Either way, the record is kept by the seller. Until a third party holds the log, every percentage on the site is his own bookkeeping.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Dr. Bob Sports is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its plays perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Dr. Bob's NFL page claims 57.5% on Best Bets since 2016. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Dr. Bob Sports is thin and mostly old. We found no Reddit discussion of the service, no Trustpilot or BBB profile we could confirm, and no recent forum threads. Below is what we did find and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: On HandicappingReviews.org, a reviewer who said he bought full season NFL and basketball packages and lost a significant sum wrote that he asked for a discount to continue and was turned down. He called Dr. Bob honest and hard working but questioned his concern for clients. Posters on this site are not verified.

Other reviews on the same page, the latest dated 1 Jan 2021, complain that lines moved before they could bet the plays, that the service is expensive for the bankroll needed, and of poor customer service. One reviewer said he lost a lot of money in four weeks.

The same page also has positive reviews: praise for customer service and for sharing methods with subscribers, and a longtime follower who said he wished he had won more but could not complain. None of these reviews give records or amounts.

A Sportsbook Review thread with an accusing title was started by a buyer who called the picks "terrible" and objected that Stoll is not a doctor. Other members replied that the nickname comes from basketball and that his results are average but he is not a fraud; one said he lost his bankroll on an earlier subscription. No logs were posted.

In a Las Vegas Advisor answer, the bettor Fezzik credited Dr. Bob with building a following by winning "without hype", then argued his results had fallen for about five years as the market caught up with his methods. This is an old opinion based on his published numbers.

In a Las Vegas Advisor forum thread on the same theme, several members respected his work but disliked how he presented his record, and one claimed he had once stopped counting the juice in a losing year. Others in the thread disagreed on whether that was dishonest. No evidence was posted and we did not verify it.
We found no Reddit thread, no Trustpilot page and no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to drbobsports.com, and no customer discussion from 2025 or 2026.

conflicts: We saw no sportsbook affiliate links, promo codes or revenue share offers on the Dr. Bob Sports pages we opened.

The NBA page sends readers to KillerCappers.com, where his former NBA handicapper now sells picks, and quotes that handicapper's recent record. We saw no statement about whether Dr. Bob Sports is paid for that referral. The NFL 4 Weeks product page also lists EVBettor as an analyst alongside Dr. Bob.
strengths: A named analyst, an LLC operator, a mailing address and a phone number, with prices and refund terms in writing.
Publishes far more than most sellers: decades of season by season records including losing years, and a weekly recap of the paid plays with the line and result.
Long free game analysis is posted for games outside the paid package, so a reader can judge the method before paying.
concerns: The record is kept by the seller, and the NFL totals differ slightly across his own pages.
No refund if the picks lose, and cancelling does not refund prepaid fees.
Old basketball package prices are still posted although the site says he is not handicapping basketball this season.
Bettors have long reported that his lines move fast after release, so a buyer may not get the posted number.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business run by Bob Stoll since 1987, with a named operator, an address, published prices and written terms. That makes it legitimate as a business; it does not prove the picks make money.
How much does Dr. Bob Sports cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 the NFL season package was $895, a price the site lowers each week as the season runs down, and the NFL 4 Weeks package was $375. Those were the only packages offered this season, and losses are not refunded.
Does Dr. Bob Sports have a verified record?

No third party verifies it. He publishes detailed season by season records and a weekly recap of the paid plays with lines, which a buyer can check going forward, but the record is kept by the seller and its totals differ slightly between his own pages.
Is Dr. Bob Sports worth it?

For the money you get every NFL Best Bet and Strong Opinion with written analysis, sent at release, from an analyst who publishes losing years as well as winning ones. What is unproven is whether those plays still beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 at the lines a buyer can actually get, and there is no refund if they do not.
